Maria: FYI customer ACME reported their March invoice jumped ~3.8x. Console shows ~120k served_tokens but invoice billed ~480k tokens. Any idea what would inflate billed tokens that much?
Dmitri: Can you paste a sample request_id and a sample payload? need to check cache hit ratio + batching traces.
Maria: request_id=r-9f2b3, sample payload attached below. They call a chat/generate with a long system prompt and short user messages, repeated many times.
Dmitri: Quick primer that usually explains this: the dashboard's 'served_tokens' is the count of tokens the model actually had to decode/generate. Billing uses our ingress metering (metered_tokens) which counts the tokens that traverse the API boundary (input + output) per request. KV/prefix cache or prefetch can reduce "served" (compute) but the bytes returned to the client are still counted by the meter. Continuous batching can also add separators or duplicated system prompts into the batch accounting, which increases metered tokens even if generation is short-circuited.
Elaine: So it's expected to see invoice > served if many responses are returned from cache?
Dmitri: Exactly. Concrete example: 100 identical requests that hit a cached 2k-token prefix — the runtime might stream those cached bytes back with no decoder work (very low generated_tokens), but the meter records ~2k tokens for each request, so billed tokens ~= 200k.
Maria: How do we reproduce/verify quickly for the customer?
Dmitri: Two quick repros:
1) Disable KV/prefix cache on the request and compare metrics. Add header `x-redwood-kv-cache: disable` and `x-redwood-debug: trace`.
2) Force cache hits by replaying the exact same prompt repeatedly and look for `cache: hit` in the trace.
You can also toggle continuous batching in the request (if using hosted flags) to see difference in batch padding/separators.
Maria: Example curl to grab debug trace and compare fields:
```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "x-redwood-debug: trace" \
  -H "x-redwood-kv-cache: disable" \
  -d '{"model":"rwl-1","input":"<...>","request_id":"r-9f2b3"}'
```
Dmitri: In the trace look for keys: `metered_tokens`, `generated_tokens`, `cache_reads`, `batch_id`. If `metered_tokens` >> `generated_tokens` and `cache_reads`>0 then the billing delta is due to cached response payloads being counted by the meter.
Jen: From billing side — policy is we bill for tokens returned to customers (including cached responses). For this customer we can offer a one-time credit while we triage. Also we should update the docs to make the difference between "metered" and "served/generation" explicit.
Elaine: Operational mitigations: warm cache ahead of peak, reduce cache TTL for churny prompts, or move heavy customers to Dedicated capacity to avoid continuous-batching pad overhead. Also can disable continuous batching for the tenant to avoid added separator tokens.
Maria: I'll prepare a short customer note explaining: (1) why invoice != dashboard served tokens, (2) how to reproduce, (3) recommended mitigations and the one-time credit.
redwood-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026 assigned to Jen (billing) — https://redwood.example/incident/INC-2026
Maria: Thanks — assigning followup to Jen and Dmitri to confirm cache metrics and run the repro against the customer's request ids.
